To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The electroosmotive flow of viscoelastic fluids in a nanoslit is investigated.
the electroosmotic velocity profiles for both the Newtonian and vischoelastic fluids are plug like and increase sharply near to the charged wall when the electric double layer is not overlapped.
the EOF of visoelastic fluid in a nanoslit is enhanced with the increasing Weissenberg number and polymer extensibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electroosmotic flows of viscoelastic fluids in nanoslits.
the EOF of vischoelastic fluid in a nanoslit.
the effect of viscoelasticity and the EDL overlapping on the EOF of a long nanoslot.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rheological property of the viscoelastic fluid has significant effect on the EOF of the LPTTs fluid in the nanoslit.
the EOF of vischoelastic fluid can be significantly enhanced compared to Newtonian fluid.
the viscoelasticity of the fluid enhances the EOF, and the effect is more pronounced for the case when the EDL thickness is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EOF of vischoelastic fluid can be enhanced through adjusting the rheological property and the degree of EDI overlapping.
the viscoelastic effect on the EOF is more significant when the EDL overlapping effect is less pronounced.
the viscoelastic fluid with larger Weissenberg and viscosity ratio numbers has higher velocity, which is consistent with the shear-thinning behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rheological properties of the LPTTs fluid can be used to manipulate the EOF of the viscoelastic fluid within a nanoslit.
viscoelastic fluids can be used to control the electroosmotic transport in nanochannels.

, for a given applied electric field, the viscoelasticity of the fluid can be tuned to enhance the EOF, which may be useful for designing microfluidic devices for drug delivery and lab-on-a-chip applications.
